page.title: Understanding Matters
page.intro: Short knowledge checks help you notice what you understand and which topics may need more explanation.

comprehension.heading: Knowledge checks
comprehension.intro: Reading information is only one part of learning. Short knowledge checks can help users identify what they understand and which topics may need further explanation.
comprehension.notDiagnostic: These checks are educational only. Answers are not used to make personal genetic-risk conclusions.
comprehension.pickTopic: Choose a topic to open a question.

feedback.retry: That is not the best answer. Read the explanation and try again.

carrier.title: Understanding carrier status
carrier.question: In general education, what does carrier status usually describe?

options.a: A confirmed diagnosis in the child
options.b: Carrying a gene variant that may be passed on, without necessarily being ill
options.c: A guarantee that a future child will be affected

carrier.explanation: Carrier status describes having a variant that can be inherited. It is not the same as a diagnosis in a child and does not guarantee an outcome.

inheritance.title: Understanding inheritance
inheritance.question: Why might both partners' results matter in couple carrier screening education?

options.a: Because inheritance patterns can involve both sides of a family
options.b: Because only one partner's genes matter legally
options.c: Because screening always replaces family history

inheritance.explanation: Couple context can help people discuss how variants may be passed on. It does not replace individual clinical interpretation.

risk_diagnosis.title: Risk versus diagnosis
risk_diagnosis.question: Which statement best reflects the difference between risk information and diagnosis?

options.a: They always mean the same thing on a report
options.b: Risk always proves a child will be affected
options.c: Risk information describes possibilities; diagnosis is a clinical conclusion about health

risk_diagnosis.explanation: Educational materials distinguish uncertainty and risk from a formal diagnosis made with professional judgement.

screening_limits.title: Understanding screening limitations
screening_limits.question: What is a common limitation of carrier screening panels?

options.a: They test every possible condition automatically
options.b: Panels vary; they may not include every condition or detect every variant type
options.c: They remove the need to discuss results with a professional

screening_limits.explanation: Panel scope and methods matter. Screening complements—not replaces—professional discussion.

counselling.title: When professional counselling may help
counselling.question: When might genetic counselling be discussed?

options.a: When people want help understanding results, uncertainty and next steps
options.b: Only when a diagnosis has already been made in a child

counselling.explanation: Counselling can support understanding and decision conversations. This product does not provide counselling on its own.

privacy.title: Privacy and consent
privacy.question: What should users expect about sharing genetic information in Rafeeq demos?

options.a: Everything is automatically shared with partners
options.c: Sharing choices should be explicit and can be limited by consent settings

privacy.explanation: Consent and sharing are user-controlled in the product design. Demo data is fictional.
